title: Field ownership registry (sync-semantics@1)
description: The machine form of docs/core/sync-semantics.md: every field that crosses a plane boundary names exactly one writing plane, the planes that receive a copy, and the planes that may never originate a write. Streams carry the watermark that makes a replay a no-op. scripts/check_sync_spec.py implements the rules this schema cannot express (one writer per field, one producer per stream, a property of the company model with no owner) and must agree with this file.

decided.description: ISO date of the decision. A field changing hands is a new major, not a new date.

planes.description: The planes that may own a field. A field naming anything else is E-SYN-05.

streams.description: One producer each. A stream with two producers is the dual write this contract exists to forbid (E-SYN-07).

fields.description: One owner each. Two fields with one id make every reference ambiguous (E-SYN-04).

plane.description: enterprise = the design plane (this repo), paperclip = execution, opengate = the tenant and its evidence, vault = the secret store.

direction.description: The only legal direction. A bidirectional stream is the rejected alternative, not a setting.

field.description: The field that carries the sequence number, e.g. `model.seq`.

monotonic.description: Strictly increasing. A wall clock is not a watermark: it can go backwards and two records can share a tick.

onReplay.description: A record at or below the stored watermark is already applied. Re-delivery is not an error.

id.description: `<stream>.<name>` — the id begins with the stream it belongs to, so a watermark (`model.seq`) is a field like any other and needs an owner.

mirroredTo.description: The planes that receive a copy. A mirror may store the field and may never author it.

neverWrittenBy.description: Every plane, other than the owner, that may not originate a write — mirrors included, because storing a copy is not writing one. A plane missing from this list has a write nobody granted (E-SYN-06).

sensitivity.description: The **data** tier from docs/core/confidentiality.md, not the industry tier: `restricted` and `classified` describe an industry's content, and a field labelled with the wrong axis reads as stricter while enforcing nothing. The checker compares this list with `metamodel/event.schema.yaml` (`pii_class`) so a fifth level cannot creep in.
